10991.correction: While loops should be used when the number of iterations can change. Even though while loops can be used in this way, for loops are a more appropriate choice as they will track the number of iterations as part of their operation.

4072.belief: Learners often get confused between the logic operators AND and OR.
4072.statement: Learners often get confused between the logic operators AND and OR.
4072.correction: For an AND statement to return True both inputs must be True. For an OR statement to return True either input can be True.

4222.belief: A list index starts at 1 as that is the first element in the list and should be counted as the first item.
4222.statement: A list index starts at 1 as that is the first element in the list and should be counted as the first item.
4222.correction: In most programming languages, list indexing is zero-based, which means the index starts at 0. The number indicates the position before the value is seen.

5087.belief: Once an item is added to a list it is fixed in to the structure of the list and it cannot be altered.
5087.statement: Once an item is added to a list it is fixed in to the structure of the list and it cannot be altered.
5087.correction: Items can be removed, inserted and amended in a list using list methods. These methods change the structure of the list. Values of items can also be updated.

9646.belief: Strings are mutable meaning that any character within the string can be changed.
9646.statement: Strings are mutable meaning that any character within the string can be changed.
9646.correction: Strings are immutable. The elements of a string cannot be changed. If changes to the string are required, the whole string must be rewritten.

4301.belief: A for loop is the same as a while loop as they are both designed to repeat instructions. You should pick one and stick to it for all your programs.
4301.statement: A for loop is the same as a while loop as they are both designed to repeat instructions. You should pick one and stick to it for all your programs.
4301.correction: Unlike a while loop, a for loop is count-controlled, meaning it will repeat a set number of times when the loop begins. In contrast, a while loop repeats instructions for as long as its condition is true. This can vary each time the loop runs.

4493.belief: Mathematical operations cannot be performed on items held in a list; the items must first be stored in a new variable.
4493.statement: Mathematical operations cannot be performed on items held in a list; the items must first be stored in a new variable.
4493.correction: Mathematical operations can be performed directly on list items by using an index value to reference the value used.

8684.belief: Python will automatically round numbers to the nearest whole number.
8684.statement: Python will automatically round numbers to the nearest whole number.
8684.correction: Python will perform calculations based on the values that have been provided and generate an answer that can include fractional parts. If you want to reduce the number of digits, you can use the round() function.

2305.belief: Detailed and complex 3D models are always created from scratch and therefore take a long time to create.
2305.statement: Detailed and complex 3D models are always created from scratch and therefore take a long time to create.
2305.correction: 3D models usually start off by using, adding and modifying simple 3D shapes. Further detail and complexities are then added to increase the realism of the model.

3146.belief: Every frame of an animation needs to be created by the animator.
3146.statement: Every frame of an animation needs to be created by the animator.
3146.correction: Most modern animations are created using tweening. Tweening creates the frames between keyframes and stitches them together. This reduces the time taken to create animations and can improve quality.

34.belief: 3D models are all made up of simple shapes that are scaled, moved and rotated.
34.statement: 3D models are all made up of simple shapes that are scaled, moved and rotated.
34.correction: Having only previously used object mode, learners may be unaware that geometry such as vertices, edges and faces can all be directly modified in edit mode. Working in edit mode gives a modeller greater freedom to create more complex models.

2100.belief: To create smooth organic surfaces and models, individual geometry such as vertices, edges and faces must be edited individually.
2100.statement: To create smooth organic surfaces and models, individual geometry such as vertices, edges and faces must be edited individually.
2100.correction: Free-form, organically shaped models can be created by using modelling tools such as proportional editing.

38.belief: The 3D viewport display in Blender is the view from the scene camera.
38.statement: The 3D viewport display in Blender is the view from the scene camera.
38.correction: What is displayed in the 3D viewport in Blender is not what is viewed from the camera. The camera view must be enabled to look through the camera and set up composition.

2306.belief: The most detailed renders should always be produced.
2306.statement: The most detailed renders should always be produced.
2306.correction: Render engines and settings should be chosen with consideration to the requirements of the project. This may include considering factors such as time constraints and hardware limitations.

2178.belief: The more data you include in a data visualisation, the better.
2178.statement: The more data you include in a data visualisation, the better.
2178.correction: Removing unneccesary data from a visualisation can improve the quality of a visualisation.

2177.belief: Data is not important when presenting findings to support an argument.
2177.statement: Data is not important when presenting findings to support an argument.
2177.correction: Data makes your point stronger by showing real evidence.

5721.belief: A positive correlation means one variable has an impact on another.
5721.statement: A positive correlation means one variable has an impact on another.
5721.correction: Just because there is a correlation, it doesn’t necessarily mean that one things causes another to increase.

2174.belief: Data capture forms are only electronic.
2174.statement: Data capture forms are only electronic.
2174.correction: A data capture form can be designed and used on paper and data can be collected in person.

4645.belief: If you have missing data and cannot find the original source, there is nothing you can do.
4645.statement: If you have missing data and cannot find the original source, there is nothing you can do.
4645.correction: You could look at similar data and generate an average value to insert. For example, if the zoo is missing a weight for a lion, they could calculate the average weight of the other lions and enter this.

10879.belief: A visualiation will always tell you the information you need to know.
10879.statement: A visualiation will always tell you the information you need to know.
10879.correction: You may need to refine or collect more data to create visualisations which answer your questions effectively.

5010.belief: The number of bits per pixel that represent the colour are always individual specific colours.
5010.statement: The number of bits per pixel that represent the colour are always individual specific colours.
5010.correction: When RGB is used to define the colour of a pixel the bits represent different intesities of red, green and blue providing different colour mixes.

3.belief: 1 bit is always used to represent 1 pixel.
3.statement: 1 bit is always used to represent 1 pixel.
3.correction: While bits are used to represent the colour of pixels, it's not always a one-to-one relationship. The number of bits used can vary depending on the colour depth of the image.

3224.belief: Generative AI always has a negative affect on society.
3224.statement: Generative AI always has a negative affect on society.
3224.correction: Generative AI isn't always negative; it depends on its use. Generative AI tools can help artists, educators and scientists create innovative designs, engaging learning materials and advanced simulations.

9334.belief: A single audio file contains only one channel of sound.
9334.statement: A single audio file contains only one channel of sound.
9334.correction: Many formats (e.g., stereo or surround sound) contain multiple channels within one file. The information contained in the audio track can be reproduced on separate channels.

498.belief: Audacity project files can be listened to on all digital devices.
498.statement: Audacity project files can be listened to on all digital devices.
498.correction: To listen to the audio on other devices, the file must be exported to a common format such as WAV (.wav) or MP3 (.mp3).

1888.belief: Compression always reduces quality or that compressed files are always lower quality than uncompressed files.
1888.statement: Compression always reduces quality or that compressed files are always lower quality than uncompressed files.
1888.correction: Lossless compression retains all original data by finding and storing repeated patterns more efficiently.

4050.belief: Laws are put in place by Parliament to stop crimes from happening.
4050.statement: Laws are put in place by Parliament to stop crimes from happening.
4050.correction: Laws don't completely stop crime, but act as a deterrent by outlining the consequences of committing crimes.

9388.belief: Social engineering involves technical skills and knowledge of computing concepts in order to carry out an attack.
9388.statement: Social engineering involves technical skills and knowledge of computing concepts in order to carry out an attack.
9388.correction: Social engineering relies on manipulating a victim to steal their personal data. This is done by finding ways to trick the user in to handing over the data willingly.

3433.belief: Hacking a computer system of someone you know as a joke is considered legal.
3433.statement: Hacking a computer system of someone you know as a joke is considered legal.
3433.correction: Even if there is no intention to commit a crime by accessing the computer system of someone you know, the fact that the access is unauthorised is considered a crime.

3290.belief: You can only get malware on a computer if you download a file.
3290.statement: You can only get malware on a computer if you download a file.
3290.correction: Malware can infect a computer in other ways, like visiting unsafe websites, clicking bad links, or through software flaws, not just by downloading files.

10733.belief: Using security measures will stop every cyber attack.
10733.statement: Using security measures will stop every cyber attack.
10733.correction: Security measures reduce the risk of cyber attacks but cannot stop all of them. New threats and advanced techniques can sometimes bypass even the best defenses.

4276.belief: As long as you use all security measures, a computer system connected to a network can be totally safe from cyber attack.
4276.statement: As long as you use all security measures, a computer system connected to a network can be totally safe from cyber attack.
4276.correction: No computer system on a network can be completely safe, even with all security measures. Cybercriminals can find new ways to attack, so security only reduces the risk and doesn't completely eliminate it.

408.belief: All artificial intelligence systems use machine learning.
408.statement: All artificial intelligence systems use machine learning.
408.correction: No, some AI systems, such as rule-based expert systems or symbolic AI, use predefined logic and heuristics rather than learning from data.

4589.belief: The micro:bit understands movement like a human does.
4589.statement: The micro:bit understands movement like a human does.
4589.correction: The micro:bit records numbers (x, y, z acceleration) that are then interpretted using programmed instructions.

10378.belief: More training makes a perfect model.
10378.statement: More training makes a perfect model.
10378.correction: Not neccessarily - models can become too specialised and fail on new data.

2173.belief: More data is always better as it means the model can be better informed to make a prediction.
2173.statement: More data is always better as it means the model can be better informed to make a prediction.
2173.correction: Poorly labelled or inconsistent data can make a model's predictions inaccurate. It is better to use a smaller amount of higher quality data to make more accurate predictions.

770.belief: Building a machine learning app just means coding as you would do with any other programming project.
770.statement: Building a machine learning app just means coding as you would do with any other programming project.
770.correction: Building a machine learning app involves data collection, model training and coding the application. These facets are integral in developing a machine learning app.

10680.belief: Users of a machine learning application do not need to be aware of how accurate it is.
10680.statement: Users of a machine learning application do not need to be aware of how accurate it is.
10680.correction: Model cards are good practice when developing machine learning applications. A model card is a short report on how a machine learning model works, how well the model performs and what people should know before using the model.

10306.correction: Not all threats are illegal, some threats do not break laws but can cause harm.

827.belief: You cannot protect your online reputation.
827.statement: You cannot protect your online reputation.
827.correction: There are many ways that you can protect your online reputation. The main way to do this is ensure you think about what you put online in the first place in the same way as you present yourself in real life.

654.belief: Big data is only for big companies or organisations.
654.statement: Big data is only for big companies or organisations.
654.correction: Businesses of all sizes can benefit from data analytics if they understand their goals and data needs.

4052.correction: Laws are used to prosecute and may deter some individuals from committing crimes, but they do not stop laws being broken in the first place.

9546.belief: There are specific laws that are designed for online crimes.
9546.statement: There are specific laws that are designed for online crimes.
9546.correction: In the UK, we don’t currently have one law that decides what is and is not illegal online. Instead something is illegal if it is illegal offline or is included as an offence in one of many pieces of legislation that govern the internet in the UK.

3789.belief: If information is on the WWW, it can be accessed by anyone in the world.
3789.statement: If information is on the WWW, it can be accessed by anyone in the world.
3789.correction: Governments in different countries restrict what can be viewed or published by the citizens within their country.

10471.belief: When two people type in the same search term into a search engine, they will get the same results.
10471.statement: When two people type in the same search term into a search engine, they will get the same results.
10471.correction: Two people could search the same term online, but based on their search history, they could receive very different results.

828.belief: You cannot protect yourself against the content you see online.
828.statement: You cannot protect yourself against the content you see online.
828.correction: There are number of steps you can take to reduce the likelihood of seeing unwanted content online, these include using safe search tools, only streaming content legally and on a secure connection and using privacy-preserving search engines.

4705.belief: Modern technology has improved individuals' working lives in all aspects.
4705.statement: Modern technology has improved individuals' working lives in all aspects.
4705.correction: There are some negative impacts of modern-day technology on the workplace and individual workers. These include fewer opportunities for face-to-face communication and 24/7 connectivity.

11118.belief: Working collaboratively is always positive and has an impact on productivity.
11118.statement: Working collaboratively is always positive and has an impact on productivity.
11118.correction: There are some disadvantages to collaborative working, for example complex decision making with multiple people can become a lengthy process and coordination of resources can be difficult.

1825.belief: Communication in the workplace is the same as communication with family or friends.
1825.statement: Communication in the workplace is the same as communication with family or friends.
1825.correction: Communication in the workplace should be formal and professional. Slang language, abbreviations and emojis should be avoided.

1729.belief: The cloud ensures everyone can access software and resources.
1729.statement: The cloud ensures everyone can access software and resources.
1729.correction: There are many different devices that can be used to access cloud services, and the functionality of each device will have an impact on the quality of service users will experience when using cloud based services.

5309.belief: PANs are limited to Bluetooth or Wi-Fi connections.
5309.statement: PANs are limited to Bluetooth or Wi-Fi connections.
5309.correction: PANs can use a variety of technologies, including wired connections like USB and FireWire, and wireless connections like Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and more.

10059.belief: Supporting an employee's mental or physical wellbeing only costs an organisation.
10059.statement: Supporting an employee's mental or physical wellbeing only costs an organisation.
10059.correction: Supporting an employee's mental or physical wellbeing can actually benefit an organisation through reduced time off and increased productivity.

10095.belief: Synchronous communication tools are better than asynchronous communication tools.
10095.statement: Synchronous communication tools are better than asynchronous communication tools.
10095.correction: Neither type of communication can be deemed better than the other overall. Some forms of communication will suit different tasks better than others.

3212.belief: Gantt charts are more effective than Kanban boards because they show project dependencies.
3212.statement: Gantt charts are more effective than Kanban boards because they show project dependencies.
3212.correction: Neither tool can be deemed more effective overall. A business should decide which of the tools will work well for them based on the needs of the project.

2228.belief: When delivering a presentation you should read the slides out word for word.
2228.statement: When delivering a presentation you should read the slides out word for word.
2228.correction: Simply reading out the slides can disengage the audience and mean that your message can become lost.

198.belief: AI can think and make decisions like humans.
198.statement: AI can think and make decisions like humans.
198.correction: AI systems have no awareness or emotions and do not think or understand in the way humans do. AI systems process data and follow patterns or rules based on training data.

3225.belief: Generative AI systems output is always accurate and based on facts.
3225.statement: Generative AI systems output is always accurate and based on facts.
3225.correction: Generative AI systems can produce convincing text but the output is not always accurate or based on facts. Fact checking is always important because AI systems generate content based on patterns in the training data, not verified information.

4027.belief: Large Language Models (LLMs) understand what they’re saying, like a human does.
4027.statement: Large Language Models (LLMs) understand what they’re saying, like a human does.
4027.correction: LLMs do not understand language or meaning. They generate responses by predicting the most likely next word based on patterns in the data they were trained on, not because they understand the content like a human does.

10496.belief: You can just type anything into an LLM and it will always give the best answer.
10496.statement: You can just type anything into an LLM and it will always give the best answer.
10496.correction: LLMs work best when you give them clear, specific and well-structured prompts. The quality of the input directly affects the quality of the output; this process of designing and refining inputs to get better results is called prompt engineering.

4682.belief: ML models are neutral and always give fair or accurate information.
4682.statement: ML models are neutral and always give fair or accurate information.
4682.correction: ML models can reflect or amplify bias in their training data. If the data contains stereotypes or imbalances, the ML model can repeat or reinforce them.

194.belief: AI image generators create completely original artwork from scratch.
194.statement: AI image generators create completely original artwork from scratch.
194.correction: AI image generators create new images by learning from and combining patterns found in millions of existing images. They don’t “imagine” or invent things like a human artist; they remix data they were trained on.

2210.belief: Deepfakes are easy to spot because they always look fake or glitchy.
2210.statement: Deepfakes are easy to spot because they always look fake or glitchy
2210.correction: Many deepfakes today are highly realistic and difficult to detect, especially when viewed quickly or shared on social media. As technology improves, deepfakes can mimic real people’s voices and faces with convincing detail.

5071.belief: Once AI is built, it can’t be changed and the risks are already set.
5071.statement: Once AI is built, it can’t be changed and the risks are already set.
5071.correction: AI systems can and should be continuously monitored, tested and improved to reduce risks. Risk mitigation is an ongoing process, not a one-time fix.

3481.belief: High-level languages are always better than low-level languages because they are easier to use.
3481.statement: High-level languages are always better than low-level languages because they are easier to use.
3481.correction: High-level languages are generally easier to learn and use. However, low-level languages offer more direct control over the computer's hardware, which can be essential for certain tasks like writing operating systems or device drivers.

460.belief: Assembly language is only used for very old computers, and it's not relevant to modern programming.
460.statement: Assembly language is only used for very old computers, and it's not relevant to modern programming.
460.correction: It's true that assembly was used more in the past, but it's still relevant. It gives direct hardware control, crucial for things like embedded systems and device drivers. Understanding it helps you see how computers work at a low level.

10602.belief: You must use an IDE to write and run programs.
10602.statement: You must use an IDE to write and run programs.
10602.correction: You don’t need an IDE to write and run programs; you can use a simple text editor and a compiler or interpreter. However, an IDE makes the process much easier by providing tools such as autocompletion and error checking.

3800.belief: Input and output of a program happen automatically, without the need for coding. The computer uses it in the correct part of your program.
3800.statement: Input and output of a program happen automatically, without the need for coding. The computer uses it in the correct part of your program.
3800.correction: Computers process instructions in code that requires input and output. The programmer needs to specify exactly where and how it should be handled.

4269.belief: As long as all the necessary lines of code are present, the program will work, regardless of their order.
4269.statement: As long as all the necessary lines of code are present, the program will work, regardless of their order.
4269.correction: Computers run code line by line, in the order it's written. If you change the sequence, you're changing the steps the computer takes, and that will change the output.

2216.belief: You can define a constant in any programming language.
2216.statement: You can define a constant in any programming language.
2216.correction: Python does not have constants. But if you want a value to be treated as a constant, it's a common naming convention for the identifier to be written in capital letters.

5235.belief: The order of instructions in a program doesn't really matter, as long as all the instructions are there.
5235.statement: The order of instructions in a program doesn't really matter, as long as all the instructions are there.
5235.correction: Computers execute code line by line, in the order it's written. If you change the sequence, you're changing the steps the computer takes, and that will change the output.

9594.belief: I can just start coding and figure it out as I go. Planning is a waste of time and boring.
9594.statement: I can just start coding and figure it out as I go. Planning is a waste of time and boring.
9594.correction: Planning is like building a strong foundation. A good plan helps you write better code faster.

10193.belief: Testing is just about making sure the program runs.
10193.statement: Testing is just about making sure the program runs.
10193.correction: It's not just about running the program. We test to make sure the program does exactly what it's supposed to do, in all situations. This means checking if it handles correct input and incorrect input correctly.

1892.belief: Computational thinking techniques are only related to solving problems with computers.
1892.statement: Computational thinking techniques are only related to solving problems with computers.
1892.correction: The underlying principles of computational thinking can be applied in various aspects of life, even without any digital technology.

218.belief: Algorithms and computer programs are actually the same thing.
218.statement: Algorithms and computer programs are actually the same thing.
218.correction: A computer program is a specific implementation of an algorithm's logic. A clearly written algorithm provides instructions that can be implemented in various ways including, but not limited to, computer programs.

3057.belief: A flowchart should always be created before writing a computer program.
3057.statement: A flowchart should always be created before writing a computer program.
3057.correction: For simple programs, a flowchart may not be needed and could add to development time. Sometimes the program code itself might be clear enough without a flowchart.

5904.belief: Pseudocode can be directly run or executed by a computer.
5904.statement: Pseudocode can be directly run or executed by a computer.
5904.correction: Pseudocode is a human-readable representation of an algorithm's logic but doesn't follow the syntax or rules of any particular programming language. It should only be used as a planning tool.

10748.belief: Using trace tables guarantees correct logic and code.
10748.statement: Using trace tables guarantees correct logic and code.
10748.correction: Trace tables can be subject to human error and can be impractical to use for complex algorithms.

387.belief: Arrays are always the best choice for storing and accessing collections of data.
387.statement: Arrays are always the best choice for storing and accessing collections of data.
387.correction: While arrays offer efficient direct access to elements using their index, they have limitations, such as fixed size and potential inefficiency in terms of unused elements.

217.belief: Algorithmic bias can be completely eliminated.
217.statement: Algorithmic bias can be completely eliminated.
217.correction: It is extremely difficult, maybe impossible, for complex algorithms to be completely free from bias. By aiming to understand sources of bias, actively working to reduce it, and being transparent, algorithmic bias can be reduced as much as possible.

1891.belief: Computational thinking means writing code for everything.
1891.statement: Computational thinking means writing code for everything.
1891.correction: While coding is a way to implement solutions, computational thinking can be applied to problems that don't require coding at all and should be seen as a set of processes that help people solve problems.

5844.belief: A program follows a sequence of instructions and will run all lines of code.
5844.statement: A program follows a sequence of instructions and will run all lines of code.
5844.correction: Selection statements can be used to control program flow, so some lines of code can be skipped to follow a different path through the program.

4155.belief: Just like addition, subtraction and multiplication there is only one type of division in programming.
4155.statement: Just like addition, subtraction and multiplication there is only one type of division in programming.
4155.correction: There are three types of division in programming; real, integer and modulo division. Each deal with remainder values differently and will be useful in different ways in programming.

5219.belief: The = operator is used for comparison.
5219.statement: The = operator is used for comparison.
5219.correction: When using Python for programming the == operator is used for comparison and the = operator is used for assignment. Other languages may not always use these operators for these tasks.

4250.belief: A logical expression can only check one value.
4250.statement: A logical expression can only check one value.
4250.correction: Logical expressions can combine relational and logical operators to check multiple values or inputs.

4924.belief: A nested selection statement can only have one nested selection block.
4924.statement: A nested selection statement can only have one nested selection block.
4924.correction: Selection statements can can continue to be nested in further selection blocks to provide more complex conditions for which specific code will be executed.

1778.belief: Comments are added to code to help you understand your program.
1778.statement: Comments are added to code to help you understand your program.
1778.correction: Comments are used to make the code more readable to a programmer who seeks to understand it. The comments should be written in a style that would help them make sense of the program.

5349.belief: All parts of a solution must be coded at the same time and tested that it works once coding has finished.
5349.statement: All parts of a solution must be coded at the same time and tested that it works once coding has finished.
5349.correction: Individual subproblems can be approached separately and tested to ensure they work before moving onto the next part. It helps to know parts of a program work as intended.

5906.belief: Pseudocode is the same as a programming language and must follow a particular syntax.
5906.statement: Pseudocode is the same as a programming language and must follow a particular syntax.
5906.correction: Pseudocode is independent of a specific programming language and does not need to follow any particular rules. All that is required is that a programmer can read the pseudocode and understand how to implement it.

5845.belief: If a program has a logic error it will not work and will give error messages.
5845.statement: If a program has a logic error it will not work and will give error messages.
5845.correction: Logic errors are errors that cause a program to work incorrectly or unexpectedly. With a logic error, the program can be run without failing, but it does not return the expected result. The user might not realise that there is an error.

2632.belief: Embedded system is a computer inside a computer / system inside a system.
2632.statement: Embedded system is a computer inside a computer / system inside a system.
2632.correction: Embedded systems are specific to a given task and often found within a machine.

1904.belief: All computers use the same operating system.
1904.statement: All computers use the same operating system.
1904.correction: Different devices can run different operating systems, for example Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS.

2087.belief: The CPU is the brain of the computer and understands the instructions received.
2087.statement: The CPU is the brain of the computer and understands the instructions received.
2087.correction: The CPU is the core of the computer system and receives instructions that it then executes with the help of the different components.

2088.belief: The CPU decodes and understands the instructions.
2088.statement: The CPU decodes and understands the instructions.
2088.correction: The instruction is decoded and then executed. The process only executes the instructions received.

8750.belief: RAM stores data and instructions when a computer is switched off.
8750.statement: RAM stores data and instructions when a computer is switched off.
8750.correction: RAM is volatile — when power is switched off, the data and instrucions are lost.

9623.belief: More storage always means a faster computer.
9623.statement: More storage always means a faster computer.
9623.correction: Upgrading from a HDD to a SSD will improve speed, but simply increasing the capacity of the same type of drive does not make the computer faster.

3726.belief: Increasing cores and clock speed improves performance.
3726.statement: Increasing cores and clock speed improves performance.
3726.correction: It can improve performance but not always, as other hardware components may not be able to work that way.

2188.belief: Data is stored "in the cloud", so it doesn't really exist physically or have an environmental cost.
2188.statement: Data is stored "in the cloud", so it doesn't really exist physically or have an environmental cost.
2188.correction: The cloud is a network of large data centres. These are real, physical facilities that consume huge amounts of energy and water, and generate significant e-waste.

4300.belief: A loop will always run at least once.
4300.statement: A loop will always run at least once.
4300.correction: A loop only runs if the condition allows it. If the condition isn’t met initially, the code inside won’t run at all.

1919.belief: The condition in a while loop is only checked once. The loop will always run a fixed number of times.
1919.statement: The condition in a while loop is only checked once. The loop will always run a fixed number of times.
1919.correction: Remind students that the condition is checked before each iteration. The loop repeats only while the condition is True. Variable changes inside the loop affect whether it continues or stops.

4078.belief: Learners may think a for loop will always repeat forever unless they manually stop it.
4078.statement: Learners may think a for loop will always repeat forever unless they manually stop it.
4078.correction: A for loop repeats a set number of times, based on the range or count value given. The loop ends automatically when the final value in the range has been reached.

4076.belief: Learners may think that the inner loop only runs once per program, rather than repeating fully each time the outer loop runs.
4076.statement: Learners may think that the inner loop only runs once per program, rather than repeating fully each time the outer loop runs.
4076.correction: The inner loop runs completely every time the outer loop runs once. This means the code inside the inner loop is repeated multiple times depending on how many times the outer loop is executed.

11130.belief: You have to write the full code for random number generation yourself.
11130.statement: You have to write the full code for random number generation yourself.
11130.correction: Python's standard library includes the random module, which already has functions like randint() to generate random numbers. You just need to import it.

5842.belief: A program will automatically ask people to try again if data is invalid.
5842.statement: A program will automatically ask people to try again if data is invalid.
5842.correction: The program will only ask for data to be input again if it has been programmed to do so; otherwise it will run with invalid data and may crash.

2844.belief: Exception handling fixes the error in the code or stops it from happening.
2844.statement: Exception handling fixes the error in the code or stops it from happening.
2844.correction: Exception handling does not prevent errors but allows the program to detect them and continue running by managing the error appropriately.

2462.belief: I don’t need to follow the project brief to draw a flowchart.
2462.statement: I don’t need to follow the project brief to draw a flowchart.
2462.correction: The project brief gives you the purpose and requirements of the program. A flowchart must reflect those to show how the program will work step by step.

3019.belief: I finished the code and it runs, so I don’t need to test it.
3019.statement: I finished the code and it runs, so I don’t need to test it.
3019.correction: Just because a program runs doesn’t mean it works correctly in all situations. Testing helps find hidden errors, especially with unusual or unexpected inputs that you might not think of.

4249.belief: All logic gates have two inputs and one output.
4249.statement: All logic gates have two inputs and one output.
4249.correction: The number of inputs depends on the logic gate. The NOT gate is different in that it only has one input.

4248.belief: As logic gates are limited to two input, logic statements should also be limited in the same way.
4248.statement: As logic gates are limited to two input, logic statements should also be limited in the same way.
4248.correction: Logic gates can be combined to created complex circuits that represent any number of logic statements combined.

706.belief: Boolean logic statements should be processed in the order they are read (from left to right).
706.statement: Boolean logic statements should be processed in the order they are read (from left to right).
706.correction: Boolean operators have an order of precedence that affects the which operator applies to which variable. If a different order is required, brackets should be used.

6561.statement: Pupils often find it difficult to know what order logic gates should be evaluated. Without brackets, there is still an order of precedence.
6561.correction: Remind pupils of how the order of precedence in maths is applied to calculations. In a similarway, logic gates should be evaluated in the order: brackets, NOT, AND, OR.

10450.belief: A truth table can only have the column headings of single inputs like A, B, or X.
10450.statement: A truth table can only have the column headings of single inputs like A, B, or X.
10450.correction: A truth table can have column headings that calculate the value of the expression, for example (A OR B).

3802.belief: Each input can only be wired to one logic gate.
3802.statement: Each input can only be wired to one logic gate.
3802.correction: Logic gates can be combined to create complex circuits that represent any number of logic statements combined. This can involve the same input being connected to multiple logic gates.

707.belief: Boolean logic is only used in logic circuits and logic gates.
707.statement: Boolean logic is only used in logic circuits and logic gates.
707.correction: The three fundamental Boolean operators are AND, OR and NOT. These are used in programs to perform selection and control program flow. In Python, these are written in words as: and, or, not.

5847.belief: A program must run line by line from top to bottom.
5847.statement: A program must run line by line from top to bottom.
5847.correction: A subrotuine is an 'out of line' block of code, which is typcially written at the top of a program and then called upon within the main program.

3194.belief: Functions and procedures are just different names for the same thing.
3194.statement: Functions and procedures are just different names for the same thing.
3194.correction: A function is a type of subroutine that returns a value whereas a procedure is a type of subroutine that does not return a value.

3193.belief: When a function returns a value it can be used throughout the program that called it.
3193.statement: When a function returns a value it can be used throughout the program that called it.
3193.correction: The return value needs to be stored if it is to be used later in the program that calls it.

461.belief: Assigning a variable inside a function automatically makes it global.
461.statement: Assigning a variable inside a function automatically makes it global.
461.correction: A variable is local, unless it is specifically set as a global variable.

8685.belief: Python has a built-in XOR operator in the same way that it has AND, OR and NOT.
8685.statement: Python has a built-in XOR operator in the same way that it has AND, OR and NOT.
8685.correction: Unlike AND, OR and NOT, Python does not have a built-in operator for XOR and instead must be designed as part of and program that uses it.

5858.belief: A project brief is a set way to solve a problem.
5858.statement: A project brief is a set way to solve a problem.
5858.correction: A project brief outlines the requirements of a system, but there may be many ways to solve the problem. The brief explains what needs to be solved, not how.

10102.belief: A system should only be tested with normal data that will be expected. If it works with normal data it will work all the time.
10102.statement: A system should only be tested with normal data that will be expected. If it works with normal data it will work all the time.
10102.correction: A system should be tested with a range of test data, including erroneous data that is not meant to be accepted. Programs should make sure that there is no way to stop the software from working if invalid inputs are entered.

1903.belief: Computers use binary for data and instructions but they can use other number systems just as easily.
1903.statement: Computers use binary for data and instructions but they can use other number systems just as easily.
1903.correction: Computers have to use binary as they are powered by electrical circuits which contain transistors which can be switched on and off using electricity. Using other number systems would require more complex circuitry.

8130.belief: The place value for binary is the same as decimal in the fact each place value to the left is 10 times greater.
8130.statement: Pupils may think the place value for binary is the same as decimal in the fact each place value to the left is 10 times greater.
8130.correction: Binary place values double. So the first bit has the place value of 1 and the second has the place value of 2 and so on.

6350.statement: Pupils will often default to decimal addition, in the fact that 1+1 = 2, whereas in binary 1+1 = 10.
6350.correction: Remind students that binary only has two digits; 0 and 1. Use the comparisons between binary and decimal addition in the slide deck to illustrate the differences.

5456.belief: When performing binary multiplication any result can be stored, regardless of how many binary digits are needed.
5456.statement: When performing binary multiplication any result can be stored, regardless of how many binary digits are needed.
5456.correction: The size of a binary number that can be stored is allocated in memory. Sometimes the result of a binary shift may result in a larger binary number that can be stored in the number of bits available.

3478.belief: Hexadecimal numbers are used to take up less memory on the computer.
3478.statement: Hexadecimal numbers are used to take up less memory on the computer.
3478.correction: Computers still only process and store binary data. Hexadecimal is used by humans to help them process long binary sequences more easily but the underlying number of bits is still the same.

2033.belief: You have to convert an 8 bit binary number in one go.
2033.statement: You have to convert an 8 bit binary number in one go.
2033.correction: As a hexadecimal digit can be represented by 4 binary digits, it is useful to convert binary numbers in nibbles (4-bits at a time). This way each digit can be converted separately and then recombined for the final value.

5218.belief: Operations in programs can only be performed on numbers.
5218.statement: Operations in programs can only be performed on numbers.
5218.correction: Operations can be performed on different types of data. What the operator does can change depending on the data type it is being used with.

3737.belief: Indexing starts at 1 as that is the location of the first element.
3737.statement: Indexing starts at 1 as that is the location of the first element.
3737.correction: In Python, and many other programming languages, indexing starts at 0.

8751.belief: The random module will only generate random numbers.
8751.statement: The random module will only generate random numbers.
8751.correction: The random module can generate random characters as well as numbers.

388.belief: Arrays and lists behave in the same way.
388.statement: Arrays and lists behave in the same way.
388.correction: An array has a predefined fixed size. A list can vary in size throughout program execution.

3190.belief: A function can only ever return one value.
3190.statement: A function can only ever return one value.
3190.correction: A list can be used to return multiple values from a function.

826.belief: You cannot print a game board or table layout neatly in Python.
826.statement: You cannot print a game board or table layout neatly in Python.
826.correction: You can added spaces and | to format a game board or table in Python.

5506.belief: You must have the physical Sense HAT device to practice coding with the Sense HAT.
5506.statement: You must have the physical Sense HAT device to practice coding with the Sense HAT.
5506.correction: You do not have to have the physical Sense HAT to try this out. The Sense HAT emulator provides a digital representation of the device.

4223.belief: A list is static, so once it is created it cannot be edited or amended.
4223.statement: A list is static, so once it is created it cannot be edited or amended.
4223.correction: A list is a dynamic data structure that can change in size. The append() function can be used to add elements to a list.

662.belief: Binary is only used to represent numerical data.
662.statement: Binary is only used to represent numerical data.
662.correction: Binary digits can be used to form sequences that can be used to represent any data. As long as it is identified what each sequence represents, binary digits can become any form of data or instructions.

447.belief: ASCII and Unicode are only used to represent the characters and symbols found in written communication across all languages in the world.
447.statement: ASCII and Unicode are only used to represent the characters and symbols found in written communication across all languages in the world.
447.correction: ASCII and Unicode include more than just characters from written languages. ASCII represents English letters, numbers and symbols. Unicode supports other symbols beyond written text, including mathematical symbols, emojis and non-text elements.

9076.belief: The same text entered into two separate text files will always result in the same file size.
9076.statement: The same text entered into two separate text files will always result in the same file size.
9076.correction: How the text has been encoded will affect the file size of a text file. ASCII uses 7 bits per character whereas Unicode uses up to 32 bits. Therefore the choice of character encoding affects the overall file size of the same text.

678.belief: Bitmap images that are large on screen are always poor quality.
678.statement: Bitmap images that are large on screen are always poor quality.
678.correction: The quality of a bitmap image depends on its resolution, not just its size on the screen. A high-resolution bitmap can appear sharp and detailed, while a low-resolution bitmap may look pixelated when enlarged.

10710.belief: Using a low resoultion or colour depth for an image makes it unusable.
10710.statement: Using a low resoultion or colour depth for an image makes it unusable.
10710.correction: A low resolution or colour depth does not necessarily make an image unusable. It depends on the purpose. Lower settings can be suitable for web use, icons or thumbnails, while higher quality is needed for printing or detailed graphics.

9081.belief: The sample rate and resolution of samples adjusts based on the sound that is being digitsed.
9081.statement: The sample rate and resolution of samples adjusts based on the sound that is being digitsed.
9081.correction: The digitsation of sound needs to be consistent so that the binary sequence represented can be processed as expected.

9432.belief: Any sound that is digitised is going to be noticeably different to the original sound.
9432.statement: Any sound that is digitised is going to be noticeably different to the original sound.
9432.correction: When sound is turned into digital form with a high enough sampling rate and sample resolution, the difference from the original sound is too small for human ears to notice.

4210.belief: A linear search can only be used on lists or sequences of numbers.
4210.statement: A linear search can only be used on lists or sequences of numbers.
4210.correction: A linear search can be used on lots of different types of data, including strings.

661.belief: A binary search can be performed on any data.
661.statement: A binary search can be performed on any data.
661.correction: A binary search can only be performed on an ordered list as it finds the expected position of the search term based on a selected mid-point in the data.

4209.belief: A linear search algorithm and binary search algorithm are equally complex to write.
4209.statement: A linear search algorithm and binary search algorithm are equally complex to write.
4209.correction: Binary search algorithms are more complex to write due to the different paths that the algorithm can take rather than stepping through the search data in order.

764.belief: The bubble sort algorithm stops on the last swap.
764.statement: The bubble sort algorithm stops on the last swap.
764.correction: The pass through the list is repeated until no more changes are made on a pass. The last pass is needed to confirm the data is in order.

4571.belief: Merge sort is the most efficient sorting algorithm for all cases.
4571.statement: Merge sort is the most efficient sorting algorithm for all cases.
4571.correction: For smaller data sets, simpler algorithms such as insertion sort or bubble sort can be faster due to the overhead in merge sort of having to break apart the data to be sorted.

765.belief: Bubble sort is a fast and efficient sorting algorithm.
765.statement: Bubble sort is a fast and efficient sorting algorithm.
765.correction: Bubble sort is considered inefficient for large data sets, but it can be made more efficient by using a flag to indicate when a swap is made in a single pass.

11193.belief: If your data is not sorted then you cannot use a binary search.
11193.statement: If your data is not sorted then you cannot use a binary search.
11193.correction: Data does need to be sorted to use a binary search, though use of a sorting algorithm first would allow binary search to be used. However, consideration must be given as to the benefit of this approach for searching.

680.belief: Bits and bytes are the same thing. They all refer to binary numbers.
680.statement: Bits and bytes are the same thing. They all refer to binary numbers.
680.correction: A bit is the smallest unit of data. A byte is a group of 8 bits and is used to summarise larger sequences of bits in a more convenient way.

1889.belief: Compression is only useful for pictures or photos.
1889.statement: Compression is only useful for pictures or photos.
1889.correction: Compression applies to many types of files such as MP3 for audio, MP4 for video, ZIP for grouped files.

4309.belief: Lossy compression always results in a poor quality file that is not as usable as the original version.
4309.statement: Lossy compression always results in a poor quality file that is not as usable as the original version.
4309.correction: Lossy compression removes data that is considered unnecessary or less noticeable, which may not impact the perceived quality of the file, especially to the human eye or ear.

3485.belief: A higher compression ratio always means better quality.
3485.statement: A higher compression ratio always means better quality.
3485.correction: A higher compression ratio actually means the file size has been reduced more. This often results in lower quality, especially with lossy compression.

9036.belief: Run length encoding always reduces file size.
9036.statement: Run length encoding always reduces file size.
9036.correction: Run length encoding only works well when data has long repeated patterns. If data is random or has frequent changes, RLE may not reduce the file size and can even make it bigger. For example, compressing "HELLO" with RLE results in "1H1E2L1O".

3548.belief: The Huffman tree is the compressed file.
3548.statement: The Huffman tree is the compressed file.
3548.correction: The compressed file is a sequence of bits, and the tree is the representation of the coding system.

633.belief: The best compression method is the one that makes files the smallest.
633.statement: The best compression method is the one that makes files the smallest.
633.correction: Smaller isn’t always better, sometimes important details are lost. The best method depends on the file type, quality needs, and purpose.

1890.belief: Compression is only useful for saving storage space.
1890.statement: Compression is only useful for saving storage space.
1890.correction: While saving storage is one benefit, compression is also critical for faster transmission of files over the internet, reducing bandwidth usage on networks, and enabling smooth real-time communication.

193.correction: AI systems follow programmed rules or improve performance based on data, but they do not think or have emotions like humans.

4334.belief: Machine learning is the same as artificial intelligence.
4334.statement: Machine learning is the same as artificial intelligence.
4334.correction: Machine learning is one of the techniques that people can use to build artificial intelligence system models. It is a subset of artificial intelligence.

3226.belief: Only generative AI systems require training data to complete tasks.
3226.statement: Only generative AI systems require training data to complete tasks.
3226.correction: All AI systems rely on training data to perform tasks by using patterns identified in the data.

197.belief: AI systems improve access to digital technologies.
197.statement: AI systems improve access to digital technologies.
197.correction: Inequality of access to AI tools and systems is an ethical concern. Not everyone has equal access to AI tools which can actually increase the digital divide.

4693.belief: A model can be improved by providing more training data.
4693.statement: A model can be improved by providing more training data.
4693.correction: Although a large data set is important, more data doesn't necessarily improve output. It is important that training data is high-quality, accurate and diverse.

10054.belief: In supervised learning, the model stores or "memorises" the training data to label new, unprocessed data.
10054.statement: In supervised learning, the model stores or "memorises" the training data to label new, unprocessed data.
10054.correction: A supervised learning model does not simply store or "memorise" training data. It detects patterns and relationships in the training data and stores these. If it only stored the training data, it could not accurately label new, unprocessed data.

1694.belief: A classifier can be improved by providing more training data.
1694.statement: A classifier can be improved by providing more training data.
1694.correction: More data doesn't always mean improved predictions. The quality of data provided to a classifier is as important as the quantity.

4933.belief: Neural networks offer transparency in terms of the decisions made by the algorithm.
4933.statement: Neural networks offer transparency in terms of the decisions made by the algorithm.
4933.correction: It’s often hard to understand why a neural network made a particular decision which makes transparency difficult.

9080.belief: The sample rate and bit depth of samples adjusts based on the sound that is being digitsed.
9080.statement: The sample rate and bit depth of samples adjusts based on the sound that is being digitsed.
9080.correction: The digitsation of sound needs to be consistent so that the binary sequence represented can be processed as expected.

4574.belief: Metadata is only used when a user needs to know when a file was made or changed.
4574.statement: Metadata is only used when a user needs to know when a file was made or changed.
4574.correction: Metadata can be used in a variety of ways. For example, software can be designed to make use of metadata for effective cataloguing and providing extra information about the properites of a file being used.

3803.belief: An insertion sort is slower than other sorting algorithms.
3803.statement: An insertion sort is slower than other sorting algorithms.
3803.correction: While other algorithms offer better time complexity for large, unsorted arrays, insertion sort can still be faster in practice for smaller and partially sorted lists.

5739.belief: A poster that is created using software is digital even when printed out.
5739.statement: A poster that is created using software is digital even when printed out.
5739.correction: The source of the design is digital if it was created using software. However, once that digital design is printed onto a physical medium like paper, the resulting poster itself becomes a physical artefact.

4141.belief: The lifecycle is a plan you follow from start to finish in sequence.
4141.statement: The lifecycle is a plan you follow from start to finish in sequence.
4141.correction: Once you get to the testing and evaluation stage, you may move back to the execution stage until you are happy with the product.

4271.belief: As long as a product is planned, it does not matter which type of planning document is used.
4271.statement: As long as a product is planned, it does not matter which type of planning document is used.
4271.correction: It is important to use the correct planning document to ensure the planning stage is useful for the creating stage.

2047.belief: Copyright only applies to the use of images.
2047.statement: Copyright only applies to the use of images.
2047.correction: Copyright refers to any creation by an original creator.

679.belief: Bitmap and raster are two different types of image.
679.statement: Bitmap and raster are two different types of image.
679.correction: They are the same and can be referred to as a raster or bitmap image.

4495.belief: It does not matter how the camera is positioned as long as the action is captured.
4495.statement: It does not matter how the camera is positioned as long as the action is captured.
4495.correction: The camera angle can help portray a key element of the moment to the viewer and help them understand the meaning of the clip.

10970.belief: Websites require specialist knowledge to create and publish.
10970.statement: Websites require specialist knowledge to create and publish.
10970.correction: Drag-and-drop software and online platforms allow anyone to create and publish a website easily.

5100.belief: Once a product is completed it does not need to be improved if I am happy with it as the creator.
5100.statement: Once a product is completed it does not need to be improved if I am happy with it as the creator.
5100.correction: Listening to other opinions and referring to the success criteria of the client brief is essential to help develop a product that meets the client brief completely.

5500.belief: Physical computing is just about programming robots.
5500.statement: Physical computing is just about programming robots.
5500.correction: Physical computing is much broader than just robotics. It includes any system where a computer interacts with the physical world through sensors and actuators, for example wearable devices, environmental sensors and smart home devices.

1977.belief: You can connect a motor directly to a microcontroller and it will work fine.
1977.statement: You can connect a motor directly to a microcontroller and it will work fine.
1977.correction: Microcontrollers send control signals, not power. Motor drivers act like electronic switches to take a signal and safely drive the motors with their own power supply.

4259.belief: As long as the components are attached the buggy will work fine.
4259.statement: As long as the components are attached the buggy will work fine.
4259.correction: A good chassis design isn’t just about holding parts. Care should be taken when positioning and securing components to ensure the buggy is reliable, easy to fix and functions as intended.

10524.belief: Ultrasonic sensors work like cameras and detect objects visually.
10524.statement: Ultrasonic sensors work like cameras and detect objects visually.
10524.correction: Ultrasonic sensors use sound not light to detect objects.

9191.belief: The sensor follows the line like a smart camera.
9191.statement: The sensor follows the line like a smart camera.
9191.correction: The sensor sends data back to the microcontroller to say whether light or dark is detected. The written code uses this data to decide how the buggy should respond.

4592.belief: The microcontroller controls all systems at the same time.
4592.statement: The microcontroller controls all systems at the same time.
4592.correction: In reality, most microcontrollers execute code sequentially, one line at a time. It may appear that microcontrollers are doing many things at once, but they’re actually switching between tasks quickly or handling them step by step.

113.belief: Adding more features always makes a product better.
113.statement: Adding more features always makes a product better.
113.correction: Adding features should be done carefully, focusing on usefulness and how well they work together to solve a problem.

10160.belief: Technical jargon impresses the audience and makes the presentation better.
10160.statement: Technical jargon impresses the audience and makes the presentation better.
10160.correction: Presentations should be clear and accessible, using simple language and examples that everyone can understand.

9565.belief: Spreadsheet formatting is only used to make a spreadsheet look attractive.
9565.statement: Spreadsheet formatting is only used to make a spreadsheet look attractive.
9565.correction: Spreadsheet formatting is used to make information clearer but is also important to ensure data values such as currency are formatted correctly.

2974.belief: The fill handle can only be used to replicate formulas.
2974.statement: The fill handle can only be used to replicate formulas.
2974.correction: The fill handle can replicate formulas, text and numbers.

1920.belief: Conditional formatting needs to be applied each time a value in a cell changes.
1920.statement: Conditional formatting needs to be applied each time a value in a cell changes.
1920.correction: Conditional formatting will automatically update if the value in a cell changes, as soon as a value meets the condition, the formatting will be appplied.

2190.belief: Data validation can only check values entered into a cell. It cannot be used to stop a user from leaving a cell blank.
2190.statement: Data validation can only check values entered into a cell. It cannot be used to stop a user from leaving a cell blank.
2190.correction: Data validation can be used to prevent users from leaving required cells blank.

3192.belief: The IF function can only return the words True or False to the user.
3192.statement: The IF function can only return the words True or False to the user.
3192.correction: The IF function returns a result of True or False, but you can set what message will be displayed to the user for each result within the function.

10497.belief: The type of chart you select doesn't matter, all charts will represent data effectively.
10497.statement: The type of chart you select doesn't matter, all charts will represent data effectively.
10497.correction: Different types of chart present different types of data effectively. For example, a pie chart is used to represent data that makes up a whole part or 100%.

4336.belief: A macro can only be used to clear data in a spreadsheet.
4336.statement: A macro can only be used to clear data in a spreadsheet.
4336.correction: A macro is used to record and repeat tasks that can be automated in a spreadsheet. They are not just used to clear or reset data.

9568.belief: A spreadsheet can only be used to explore the costs of the event after it has happened.
9568.statement: A spreadsheet can only be used to explore the costs of the event after it has happened.
9568.correction: A spreadsheet model can be used to predict and model the costs of the event before it happens to help the organisers make decisions about income and expenditure.

2066.belief: The COUNTIF function is the same as the COUNT function.
2066.statement: The COUNTIF function is the same as the COUNT function.
2066.correction: A COUNTIF function returns the total number of cells based on a set criterion, whereas the COUNT function returns the number of cells that contain a number in a range.

5859.belief: Project management will not alter the outcome of a project or make it a success.
5859.statement: Project management will not alter the outcome of a project or make it a success.
5859.correction: Project management will not guarantee success of a project, but effective project management will increase the likelihood of a project being successful.

2943.belief: A feasibility report outlines the key requirements of a system.
2943.statement: A feasibility report outlines the key requirements of a system.
2943.correction: A feasibility report is a document used in project management that assesses whether a project can be completed successfully.

3820.belief: Interaction can only occur between consecutive stages of the project lifecycle.
3820.statement: Interaction can only occur between consecutive stages of the project lifecycle.
3820.correction: Interaction can happen across multiple stages of the project lifecycle.

3211.belief: Gantt charts are better than PERT charts.
3211.statement: Gantt charts are better than PERT charts.
3211.correction: Gantt charts may be deemed better than PERT charts in some instances, but not all. The choice of chart can depend on the project and what the team prefers to use.

3135.belief: Formulas can only be used on cells within one worksheet in a spreadsheet.
3135.statement: Formulas can only be used on cells within one worksheet in a spreadsheet.
3135.correction: Formulas can work across multiple worksheets in a spreadsheet.

643.belief: It is better to check that hyperlinks work each time you add a link instead of checking them at the end.
643.statement: It is better to check that hyperlinks work each time you add a link instead of checking them at the end.
643.correction: You should check the hyperlinks as you go to fix errors immediately but also check the whole product is working once you have finished. This will ensure that the product meets the brief and works in its entirety.

4042.belief: The last stage of the project evaluation is the conclusion.
4042.statement: The last stage of the project evaluation is the conclusion.
4042.correction: The last stage of the project evaluation is "recommendations". It is important to reflect on and learn from your experiences and say what could be improved and how.

825.belief: You cannot prevent things from going wrong in a project.
825.statement: You cannot prevent things from going wrong in a project.
825.correction: Things can be done to prevent negative things happening during a project - these are called mitigations.

10629.belief: You should use all planning tools (Gantt, PERT and feasibility reports).
10629.statement: You should use all planning tools (Gantt, PERT and feasibility reports).
10629.correction: You don't need to use all planning tools; select the tools most suitable for a project.

10189.belief: Testing should only be done at the end of a project.
10189.statement: Testing should only be done at the end of a project.
10189.correction: It is good practice to test products during and at the end of a project.

10952.belief: There is no way to store multiple records in one data structure in Python.
10952.statement: There is no way to store multiple records in one data structure in Python.
10952.correction: If you want to use multiple records in a database, then you can add multiple dictionaries to a list.

2337.belief: A dictionary is a static data structure meaning you cannot add or remove items, only change the values that are available.
2337.statement: A dictionary is a static data structure meaning you cannot add or remove items, only change the values that are available.
2337.correction: A dictionary is a dynamic data structure, which means you can add or remove items in the data structure during program execution.

5733.belief: It is not possible to interrogate a CSV file in Python without importing a specialised library.
5733.statement: It is not possible to interrogate a CSV file in Python without importing a specialised library.
5733.correction: A CSV file behaves in the same way as a txt file in Python. Data is read from the file as strings and methods can be used to remove extra characters like commas, spliting the values either side in to separate items.

11131.belief: You can write integers directly to a CSV file using file.write(number).
11131.statement: You can write integers directly to a CSV file using file.write(number).
11131.correction: All data must be converted to strings before writing.

5124.belief: There is only one correct solution to a problem when programming.
5124.statement: There is only one correct solution to a problem when programming.
5124.correction: There are lots of different approaches to solving a problem in programming. Some solutions can work better than others but the first stage in getting a solution is ensuring that it provides the expected outputs that are required.

5857.belief: A project brief always includes success criteria.
5857.statement: A project brief always includes success criteria.
5857.correction: Sometimes a project brief may not include success criteria, but a brief description of what the program needs to do. You may need to generate success criteria from the project brief.

5101.belief: Once a program has been developed, it is finished and there is no need to evaluate or reflect on what you have done.
5101.statement: Once a program has been developed, it is finished and there is no need to evaluate or reflect on what you have done.
5101.correction: Evaluation is about judging how well the program meets the original success criteria or requirements. It can help you to revisit and make improvements to a program, as well as reflect on lessons learnt for your next project.

4932.belief: All networks must have a server because a server is always needed to share files or printers between devices.
4932.statement: All networks must have a server because a server is always needed to share files or printers between devices.
4932.correction: Not all networks need a server. In a peer-to-peer model, each computer can act as both client and server, sharing files directly. This setup is simpler but may lack central control and security.

2322.belief: All devices in a network do the same thing, they just send and receive data.
2322.statement: All devices in a network do the same thing, they just send and receive data.
2322.correction: In a client–server network, devices have different roles. Servers provide services like file storage or email. Clients request and use those services, rather than providing them.

2323.belief: All devices on a network share the same MAC address because they’re connected to the same router.
2323.statement: All devices on a network share the same MAC address because they’re connected to the same router.
2323.correction: Each network device has its own unique MAC address assigned to its network interface card (NIC).

4931.belief: All network topologies work the same way and have the same benefits.
4931.statement: All network topologies work the same way and have the same benefits.
4931.correction: Different topologies connect devices in different ways. For example, star networks use a central hub, while mesh networks connect devices directly. Each has unique strengths and weaknesses depending on the situation.

11032.belief: All wired networks use the same type of cable.
11032.statement: All wired networks use the same type of cable.
11032.correction: Copper Ethernet and fibre optic cables have different speeds, distances and uses. For example, copper Ethernet is fine for short distances, but fibre optic is better for fast, long-distance connections.

11033.belief: Wireless networks are always better than wired ones because they don’t use cables.
11033.statement: Wireless networks are always better than wired ones because they don’t use cables.
11033.correction: Wireless is more convenient, but it can be slower, less secure and more prone to interference. Wired connections are often better for speed, stability and data heavy tasks.

2324.belief: All devices on a network use the same IP address, so there’s no need for private or public IPs or DNS.
2324.statement: All devices on a network use the same IP address, so there’s no need for private or public IPs or DNS.
2324.correction: Each device needs a unique private IP address on a local network. To access the internet, the router uses a public IP address. DNS translates website names into IP addresses so devices know where to send data.

2896.belief: The only factor that affects network performance is how fast your internet connection is.
2896.statement: The only factor that affects network performance is how fast your internet connection is.
2896.correction: Connection speed does affect performance, but it is also influenced by factors like bandwidth, latency, number of users, packet loss, hardware quality and interference on wireless networks.

4927.belief: Network failure just means the internet stops working for a bit; it’s annoying but not serious.
4927.statement: Network failure just means the internet stops working for a bit; it’s annoying but not serious.
4927.correction: Network failure can lead to data loss, financial damage and safety risks in sectors like healthcare. It is more than just an inconvenience and can impact lives and businesses.

5536.belief: Planning isn't needed for coding projects — you can just develop your code as you write.
5536.statement: Planning isn't needed for coding projects — you can just develop your code as you write.
5536.correction: If you plan out your algorithm first in human language, you can ensure each part is correct before writing any actual code. This reduces the likelihood of logic errors which could stop your code working as expected.

2460.belief: You don't need to consider the inputs, outputs and processes of a program during the analysis stage.
2460.statement: You don't need to consider the inputs, outputs and processes of a program during the analysis stage.
2460.correction: Listing the inputs, processes and outputs before coding helps you clearly understand what the program needs to do, avoid mistakes and save time later. It breaks the problem into smaller steps, making it easier to solve and explain to others.

2311.belief: If you are developing code for a project on your own, you don't need to worry about software design principles.
2311.statement: If you are developing code for a project on your own, you don't need to worry about software design principles.
2311.correction: Even if your code isn't used by others, it is a good idea to follow software design principles in case you have to revisit or develop your code later on.

5905.belief: Pseudocode can be executed by a computer.
5905.statement: Pseudocode can be executed by a computer.
5905.correction: Pseudocode cannot be executed by a computer. Pseudocode must be translated into a real programming language such as Python, Java or C# for it to be executed by a computer.

342.belief: The append() method will replace the existing contents of a list.
342.statement: The append() method will replace the existing contents of a list.
342.correction: The append() method will add an item to the end of an existing list but it will not replace or overwrite any existing items in a list.

3191.belief: A function and a procedure are the same.
3191.statement: A function and a procedure are the same.
3191.correction: A function is different from a procedure because it returns a value or values to the main program.

10197.belief: Testing is something you only do at the end of a project.
10197.statement: Testing is something you only do at the end of a project.
10197.correction: Testing is carried out throughout the development process. There are also specific stages and methods of testing that can be adopted. An overall approach to testing should be agreed and planned depending on the requirements of the system.

10186.belief: A test plan should only include data that will cause a program to not work.
10186.statement: A test plan should only include data that will cause a program to not work.
10186.correction: A test plan should contain a range of test data, including normal, erroneous and boundary.

2778.belief: An evaluation just states if something works or not.
2778.statement: An evaluation just states if something works or not.
2778.correction: A strong evaluation should be specific and evidence-based, covering what works, how this was achieved and how it was tested.

11128.belief: The World Wide Web is a single entity stored in one place.
11128.statement: The World Wide Web is a single entity stored in one place.
11128.correction: The World Wide Web is a vast collection of interconnected websites and documents hosted on servers all over the world. Your web browser accesses these different locations to display the information you see.

2191.belief: All the data from a website travels together in one file and always takes the same route through the internet to reach your device.
2191.statement: All the data from a website travels together in one file and always takes the same route through the internet to reach your device.
2191.correction: Data is broken into packets, and each packet may take a different route. This makes transmission faster and more reliable, because the network can avoid delays or busy routes.

2319.belief: Devices automatically know how to communicate to any other device, regardless of brand or type, without needing specific rules.
2319.statement: Devices automatically know how to communicate to any other device, regardless of brand or type, without needing specific rules.
