2319.correction: Devices rely on shared protocols to communicate and exchange data effectively, like a common language or set of rules. This ensures all devices follow the same process.

3830.belief: The internet is built directly on the OSI 7-layer model, and its layers are actual physical hardware components.
3830.statement: The internet is built directly on the OSI 7-layer model, and its layers are actual physical hardware components.
3830.correction: The OSI model is a conceptual framework, not the internet's direct architecture. It helps to understand network functions.

9923.belief: Protocols like HTTP or FTP operate at all layers, or that TCP and IP are the only protocols in the model.
9923.statement: Students may think protocols like HTTP or FTP operate at all layers, or that TCP and IP are the only protocols in the model.
9923.correction: Specific protocols perform unique functions at dedicated TCP/IP layers.

2463.belief: You don’t need any hardware for the cloud — everything just happens online.
2463.statement: You don’t need any hardware for the cloud — everything just happens online.
2463.correction: The cloud still relies on physical hardware, like servers, storage devices and networking equipment.

9149.belief: Search engines instantly know every website and search live each time you type in a query.
9149.statement: Search engines instantly know every website and search live each time you type in a query.
9149.correction: Search engines don’t search the web in real time. They use crawlers to index content in advance. When you search, they quickly scan this index to return the most relevant results.

4930.belief: Network threats and attacks come only from external hackers or from sources outside a network, while internal users or trusted software pose no risk.
4930.statement: Network threats and attacks come only from external hackers or from sources outside a network, while internal users or trusted software pose no risk.
4930.correction: Threats can be internal, like careless employees or malicious insiders, as well as external.

4928.belief: Network security just stops viruses, so it’s only important for large organisations, not for individuals or small businesses.
4928.statement: Network security just stops viruses, so it’s only important for large organisations, not for individuals or small businesses.
4928.correction: Network security protects all users, not just large organisations. It prevents data theft, fraud, and service disruption. Individuals need protection from threats like phishing or ransomware.

5804.belief: A primary key and a foreign key are the same thing.
5804.statement: A primary key and a foreign key are the same thing.
5804.correction: A primary key is an attribute that uniquely identifies a record in a database table, whereas a foreign key is an attribute in one table that is the primary key in another table and is used to link the tables together.

2195.belief: A DBMS is only used for storing data.
2195.statement: A DBMS is only used for storing data.
2195.correction: While storage is a major function, a DBMS also provides data security, integrity and querying capabilities.

2227.belief: You can delete data from a database using an SQL command without any consideration.
2227.statement: You can delete data from a database using an SQL command without any consideration.
2227.correction: You should delete data using SQL commands carefully as data may be linked to other tables in the database.

10734.belief: Using SELECT * is always the best method for returning data from a database table.
10734.statement: Using SELECT * is always the best method for returning data from a database table.
10734.correction: You should only use the SELECT * query when all fields are needed. Including unnecessary data can be frustrating for the person viewing and working with the results.

9576.belief: SQL statements can only be used with exisiting tables.
9576.statement: SQL statements can only be used with exisiting tables.
9576.correction: SQL statements can be used to perform other actions on a databse such as creating new tables.

5887.correction: Proprietary software is usually sold to end users, although sometimes it is available for free.

5077.belief: Once data is stored in a database, it’s automatically safe and private.
5077.statement: Once data is stored in a database, it’s automatically safe and private.
5077.correction: Just storing data in a database does not make it secure. Data must be protected with proper privacy measures.

655.belief: Big data can be stored in normal data strcutures like relational databases.
655.statement: Big data can be stored in normal data strcutures like relational databases.
655.correction: Big data is mostly unstructured, so it doesn't fit the row-and-column format of relational databases.

583.belief: Because data is stored in the cloud, it doesn’t have a physical or environmental impact.
583.statement: Because data is stored in the cloud, it doesn’t have a physical or environmental impact.
583.correction: The term "cloud" sounds invisible, so many people assume their photos, videos and files are floating around in some harmless digital space. But in reality the cloud is made up of millions of physical data centres which are based across the world.

3432.belief: All hackers are criminals trying to steal or destroy data.
3432.statement: All hackers are criminals trying to steal or destroy data.
3432.correction: Not all hackers are malicious. There are different types of hackers such as white hat ethical hackers, grey hat hackers who may break rules but not for personal gain and black hat hackers who are malicious hackers who exploit systems illegally.

9387.belief: Social engineering only involves technical hacking or complex cyberattacks.
9387.statement: Social engineering only involves technical hacking or complex cyberattacks.
9387.correction: Social engineering mainly targets human psychology, not technical vulnerabilities. It's more about exploiting trust and human error than technical skills.

4404.belief: Malware only affects computers, not phones or tablets.
4404.statement: Malware only affects computers, not phones or tablets.
4404.correction: Malware can infect any idevice that is connected to the internet, including smartphones, tablets and smart TVs. Mobile malware is increasingly common and can steal data, track location or lock users out of their devices — just like on computers.

3811.belief: Installing antivirus software is enough to fully protect my device from malware.
3811.statement: Installing antivirus software is enough to fully protect my device from malware.
3811.correction: Antivirus software is helpful, but it’s only one part of a broader defence strategy. Full protection also requires regular software updates, strong passwords, safe browsing habits and user awareness to avoid phishing and suspicious downloads.

2648.belief: Encryption makes data completely safe and unbreakable.
2648.statement: Encryption makes data completely safe and unbreakable.
2648.correction: Encryption greatly improves security, but it is not foolproof. If encryption keys are weak, stolen or mismanaged, encrypted data can still be accessed by attackers.

1665.belief: Ciphers and encryption are the same thing.
1665.statement: Ciphers and encryption are the same thing.
1665.correction: Ciphers are one type of encryption method. Encryption includes ciphers but also involves algorithms, keys, and protocols used in modern digital security systems.

5384.belief: Penetration testing is illegal or the same as hacking.
5384.statement: Penetration testing is illegal or the same as hacking.
5384.correction: Penetration testing is legal and ethical when done with permission. It's a form of ethical hacking used to help organisations find and fix security weaknesses before real hackers exploit them.

2918.belief: Fake news is easy to spot because it’s obviously false or silly.
2918.statement: Fake news is easy to spot because it’s obviously false or silly.
2918.correction: Fake news is often designed to look real and believable. It can mimic trusted sources, use partial truths, or appeal to emotions to trick people. It’s important to check information sources and think critically, even if a post seems convincing.

2151.belief: Cybersecurity jobs are only for highly technical people who know how to code or hack.
2151.statement: Cybersecurity jobs are only for highly technical people who know how to code or hack.
2151.correction: Cybersecurity careers are diverse, and many roles value communication, analytical thinking, problem solving and ethical judgment just as much as technical skills.

3546.correction: HTML is a markup language. It defines the structure and appearance of content on a web page, but does not not do any processing of data into information.

9425.belief: If someone cannot view an image on a web page it can be ignored as text on the page will be sufficient.
9425.statement: If someone cannot view an image on a web page it can be ignored as text on the page will be sufficient.
9425.correction: Images are used in web pages to provide the reader with extra context. By not describing them in some way the reader might not understand the information in the same way than if it was viewed.

10679.belief: Users don't ever see the underlying file structure of a website, so it's organisation is unimportant.
10679.statement: Users don't ever see the underlying file structure of a website, so it's organisation is unimportant.
10679.correction: Organisation of resources can make the creation and maintainence of websites an easier task. The quicker a developer of website can find the component parts, the less time will be wasted when changes need to be made.

2560.belief: It is easier to apply CSS directly to the HTML tags as they are used.
2560.statement: It is easier to apply CSS directly to the HTML tags as they are used.
2560.correction: There is little time saved by applying CSS directly to tags and it generates more work later if the same changes need to be made in different parts of a web page.

10966.belief: Web page divisions all need to have unique labels. They can't be the same.
10966.statement: Web page divisions all need to have unique labels. They can't be the same.
10966.correction: When designing divisions of a web page the same formatting may need to be applied to multiple divisions. In this case the labels would need to be the same.

2434.belief: Divisions can only be arranged as regular rows and columns.
2434.statement: Divisions can only be arranged as regular rows and columns.
2434.correction: By using divisions within other divisions any layout of a page is possible.

3907.belief: JavaScript changes the original HTML file.
3907.statement: JavaScript changes the original HTML file.
3907.correction: JavaScript only changes what the user sees in the browser. It does not change the actual HTML file saved on your computer or server.

2473.belief: I don’t need a wireframe or site map, I can just start coding.
2473.statement: I don’t need a wireframe or site map, I can just start coding.
2473.correction: Planning is a key step in web development. A wireframe helps you decide where things go before writing any code, and a site map ensures you know how pages connect. Skipping planning often leads to messy code and confusing navigation.

3908.belief: JavaScript only works after everything is perfect, I’ll fix it all at the end.
3908.statement: JavaScript only works after everything is perfect, I’ll fix it all at the end.
3908.correction: JavaScript is best written and tested in small steps. Writing a little, testing it, and debugging as you go helps avoid big problems later.

10202.belief: A text file can be stored anywhere to be used in a program using just the file name.
10202.statement: A text file can be stored anywhere to be used in a program using just the file name.
10202.correction: A text file must be stored in the same location as a program to be used to be accessed by file name alone. If it is stored elsewhere, the full path of the file will also need to be included.

2098.belief: You have to create a new write() line for each line you want to add to a file.
2098.statement: You have to create a new write() line for each line you want to add to a file.
2098.correction: You can write mutiple lines in one write() statement. But if you want the text to appear on separate lines, you must use the new line character.
